dish: Island awamori (c. 400 labels incl. rare remote-island brands) served in Okinawan pottery vessels such as karakara and chibugwā
n: Ryūkyū no Shuki to Awamori Oninoude, Tsuboya (琉球ノ酒器ト泡盛 オニノウデ)
w: Awamori bar opened in July 2016 by sake-vessel collector Sakukawa Nagamasa, about 10 minutes' walk from Kokusai-dōri toward the Nōren market; some 400 awamori, many from the outer islands, poured from Okinawan karakara/chibugwā flasks and works by noted potters. Named for the long 'ogre's arm' bottle of old Ryūkyū; picked in BRUTUS's Naha bar issue.

dish: Old-style Okinawan breads — wiener rolls, age-pan, curry bread, anpan — plus the 'omiso melon pan' made with Shuri miso; ¥ bread buffet
n: Kinjō Bakery, Shuri (金城ベーカリー)
w: Neighbourhood bakery founded in 1952 by Kinjō Mutsuhide, a minute from Gibo monorail station, still baking about 50 kinds of nostalgic breads; added an 'omiso melon pan' using miso from Shuri's royal-era Tamanahauso. Eat-in space runs a one-hour bread buffet.

dish: Awamori with Okinawan izakaya plates and a closing bowl of soba (shime)
n: Sakaemachi Bottleneck (栄町ボトルネック)
w: Shōwa-mood sakaba in a former house down an alley at the west entrance of Sakaemachi Market, credited as one of the core shops of the 'second Sakaemachi boom' that drew a younger crowd to the post-war market; awamori, Okinawan snacks and a soba to finish.

dish: Thick-cut 'tonteki' of Okinawan pineapple pork, with awamori chosen by an in-house awamori master
n: Okinawan Restaurant Jimanya, Naha (じまんや 那覇店)
w: Okinawan restaurant in a renovated 50-year-old Okinawan house about five minutes from Miebashi station, cooking with Okinawa-raised pineapple pork and island vegetables; signature thick pork-loin tonteki, and an awamori master picks a label to suit you. English menu.

dish: Daitō soba — thick, wavy hand-rolled noodles in pork broth — with Daitō-zushi (marinated-fish island sushi)
n: Daitō Soba Kokusai-dōri (大東そば 国際通り店)
w: Near Midorigaoka Park off Kokusai-dōri, the one place in Naha serving the Minami-Daitō Island soul food: thick curly noodles meant to evoke the island's rough seas, in a light pork broth, with Daitō-zushi. The owner spent a year recreating the original shop's recipe after it closed in 2022 and kept its logo.

dish: Okinawa soba in a cloudy white pork-bone broth (originally the 10-cent kamaboko-negi-ginger soba)
n: Mutsumibashi Kadoya (むつみ橋かどや) — CLOSED
address: Mutsumibashi, off Kokusai-dōri, Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
w: Okinawa soba specialist founded in 1952 by Ishikawa Yasushiro near Kokusai-dōri, which began selling a single kamaboko-and-ginger soba for 10 cents, once ran 24 hours and took students' watches as IOUs; known for its cloudy pork-bone broth. Closed on 20 June 2024 after 72 years.

dish: Seasonal-fruit cocktails (e.g. Okinawan mikan) and awamori-based Okinawan cocktails
n: BAR Owl, Kumoji (バー オウル)
w: Cocktail bar in Naha's Kumoji business district behind a heavy door, with a counter lined with tropical fruit; known for showy seasonal-fruit cocktails such as Okinawan mikan, and awamori cocktails. Selected for Tabelog's Bar 100 (2022).
